story.head: The Islanders need a win
paras: The Kings won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in overtime on Long Island on Oct 22. The Kings (5-9-2) lost 3-0 to Nashville on Tuesday, and the Islanders are winless in four (0-2-2). Going in, the Isles are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Kings seventh in the Pacific (30th).

The Islanders’ record (.529) is about what their chances are worth. The Kings have played better than their record (.375) says: their chances are worth about .617, and their finishing has held them back.

The Islanders get their defensemen shooting (1st), have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd) and spread the ice time through the lineup (3rd). As for the Kings, they keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (3rd) and keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest). They also leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), so the Islanders’ defensemen shoot a lot, and theirs not so much. Both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Bo Horvat (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 17 GP) is tied for the Islanders’ scoring lead. Matthew Schaefer (5 G / 12 A / 17 P in 17 GP) shares it. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and ten goals in 13 games against the Islanders since 2023-24. Adrian Kempe (6 G / 7 A / 13 P in 15 GP) is next in line.

Ilya Sorokin (6-4-2 / .914 SV% in 12 GS) has been terrific for the Islanders and is expected to start. Darcy Kuemper (5-4-1 / .878 SV% in 10 GS) is expected to go for Los Angeles. Kuemper has a .933 save percentage in seven starts against the Islanders, well above his usual .899. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Peter Laviolette likes to send Moore, Byfield and Perry out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Holmström, Horvat and Palmieri.
